text: A privacy impact assessment is a structured review of a planned data processing activity, done before it launches, to identify privacy risks and decide how to address them in advance. This closing lesson covers what one actually contains.

GDPR's Article 35 requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment specifically when processing is likely to result in a high risk to individuals — large-scale sensitive data processing and systematic monitoring are the examples the regulation calls out. Not every project needs the formal version, but the practice is useful far more broadly.

A usable assessment answers the same core questions regardless of template. What data, and why, exactly. Is it necessary and proportionate — could the same purpose be met with less. What are the actual risks to individuals, not just 'could we get breached.' What mitigates those risks. And who signed off, confirming it was genuinely done.

Run Lesson 28's dashboard project through this, and 'what data, and why' alone would have surfaced that a regional sales dashboard didn't need row-level customer records at all. 'Necessary and proportionate' would have flagged the broad access grant before it was ever made — caught at design time, not three months later during a recertification cycle.

That closes Data Security, Privacy & Classification. Congratulations on finishing all thirty lessons — classify before you expose, grant the minimum, log what happened, know your obligations before an incident forces you to learn them. The Data Governance path continues next with Microsoft Purview, where many of these ideas get implemented hands-on in a real enterprise governance tool.
